question.text: Will Donald Trump's approval rating reach a new low in the second half of December 2026?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question resolves as **Yes** if Donald Trump's approval rating after December 15, 2026 and before January 1, 2027 reaches an approval level strictly lower than any Trump second presidential term level before that time period, according to Nate Silver's [Do Americans approve or disapprove of Donald Trump?](https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin) tracker.

For example, on July 22, 2026, the lowest approval rating according to the resolution source was 38.29062, reported for May 21, 2026. Thus, a question asked on July 22, 2026 would require Trump's approval rating to be below that level in order to resolve as Yes.
question.fine_print: Between the value shown in the chart and the csv file under the chart ("Get the data"), the csv file takes precedence. See the "approve" column in the csv. The question resolves based on the values shown when checked by Metaculus on or after the resolution date and will not be re-resolved in case of a later update to the resolution source.

# Trump approval: will the Silver Bulletin tracker hit a new low between Dec 16 and Dec 31, 2026?

**Short answer:** Nothing has settled this yet. The record to beat is **36.25311 (Oct 21, 2026)**. The latest reading is **37.16927 (Nov 17)**, so approval needs to fall about another 0.92 points, on some day from Dec 16 to Dec 31.

## 1. Resolution source
- The tracker page embeds Datawrapper chart kSCt4. Its latest version (8787) has this CSV: [dataset.csv](https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/kSCt4/8787/dataset.csv). Columns are modeldate, approve, disapprove, plus lo/hi bands.
- 2026-11-17: approve **37.16927**, disapprove 59.8534. This is the latest row. [CSV](https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/kSCt4/8787/dataset.csv)
- **Second-term low so far: 36.25311 on 2026-10-21.** The only other values starting with 36 are 36.46 (Oct 22), 36.88 to 36.89 (Oct 23 to 25) and 36.64 (Oct 9 to 10). [CSV](https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/kSCt4/8787/dataset.csv)
- The May 21 value of 38.29062 cited in the question still matches the CSV, so past rows do not seem to have been revised.
- 2026-11-17: the page text says "Today, 37 percent of Americans approve... 60 percent disapprove", with strong approval at 18.9%. [Silver Bulletin](https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin)

## 2. Current status
- Not settled. A Yes needs a daily value **below 36.25311** dated Dec 16 to Dec 31, about 0.92 points under the Nov 17 level.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16/17: Reuters/Ipsos (Nov 13 to 16, n=1,521) has approval at 32% and disapproval at 66%. That is the fourth straight reading of about 32%, after the series low of 31% in mid-October. The poll ties the low numbers to the Iran war and fuel prices. [Democrat & Chronicle](https://eu.democratandchronicle.com/story/news/2026/11/17/donald-trump-approval-rating-latest-polls/92824140007/), [GV Wire](https://gvwire.com/2026/11/16/trump-approval-holds-near-career-low-at-32-reuters-ipsos-poll-finds/)
- 2026-11-16: Economist/YouGov (Nov 9 to 11) has 32/63, a record low for that series. [HNGN](https://www.hngn.com/articles/273849/20261116/trump-hits-record-low-32-yougov-averages-sit-higher.htm)
- Early November: Emerson (Nov 3 to 4) has approval at 41%, down from 45%. Pollsters disagree widely. [search summary](https://newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-falling-midterm-losses-12709719)
- 2026-11-03: Democrats won both chambers in the midterms. They take control on Jan 3. [Democrat & Chronicle](https://eu.democratandchronicle.com/story/news/2026/11/17/donald-trump-approval-rating-latest-polls/92824140007/)
- 2026-10-21: the average hit its new low of about 36%. [political.org](https://political.org/2026/10/21/trump-approval-hits-new-low-at-36-two-weeks-before-midterms-polls-show/)

## 4. Base rates and variation (from the CSV)
- The trend is down. The average was about 41 to 42 in Jan to Mar 2026, about 39 in Apr to Jul, about 38.2 in Aug, and about 37 to 37.5 from late September on.
- New lows were set in May, Aug, Sep, Oct 9 and Oct 21. That is roughly one new low every one to two months over the past six months.
- Monthly swings run about 1 to 2 points:
  - Sep 18 to Oct 21: 38.49 down to 36.25 (−2.2).
  - Oct 21 to Nov 2: up to 38.35 (+2.1), including a one-day jump of +1.1 on Nov 2.
  - Nov 2 to Nov 17: back down to 37.17.
- Values stay flat on weekends and other days with few polls. Holiday polling in late December is usually sparse, which could keep the line flat.
- Since Oct 21 the series has not gone below 36.46.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not confirm which approval source the Kalshi markets resolve on, and their prices may not match the Silver Bulletin series.
- **Kalshi, "How low before 2027?" (Dec 2025 to Dec 2026):**
  - Below 36%: 0.57
  - Below 35.5%: 0.40
  - Below 35%: 0.21
  - Below 34%: 0.12
- **Kalshi, "How low during his term?" (to Jan 2029):** below 36%: 0.94.
- **Kalshi, VoteHub approval on Nov 20:** the most likely band is 37.5 to 37.7 (0.36), and below 37.5 is 0.25.
- **Polymarket, "How low in 2026?":** 37% has resolved Yes. 35% is at 0.13, and 30% at 0.026.
- **Polymarket, Nov 20 level:** the most likely band is 38.0 to 38.4 (0.52), and below 38.0 is 0.21. That is higher than the Silver Bulletin's 37.17, so it probably uses a different source. I did not verify this.
- **Manifold:** there is an ACX market on net approval on Dec 31, 2026 ([link](https://manifold.markets/DaftPunkRock/acx-2026-what-will-be-donald-trumps)), but I could not get its values.
- I found no expert forecast on this exact question.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- **Dec 11, 2026: government funding runs out** under the September stopgap. Kalshi has priced a shutdown starting Dec 12 at about 43.8%. Democrats are weighing using this deadline as leverage over the Iran war. [Kalshi News](https://news.kalshi.com/p/government-shutdown-odds-december-2026-43-percent), [roic.ai](https://www.roic.ai/news/us-shutdown-risk-rises-as-democrats-weigh-using-funding-deadline-to-challenge-iran-war-11-09-2026)
- **Iran war:** war funding was put off to the December lame-duck session. Reports say fighting has resumed and gas prices are rising, but these reports conflict and are not up to date. [NOTUS](https://www.notus.org/congress/trump-resumed-the-iran-war-republicans-are-rattled), [Punchbowl](https://punchbowl.news/article/defense/iran-trump-gop/)
- **Holidays:** fewer polls come out during Thanksgiving and late December, which could leave the average flat.
- **Jan 3, 2027:** the Democratic Congress is seated, after the resolution window closes.

Sources: [Silver Bulletin](https://www.natesilver.net/p/trump-approval-ratings-nate-silver-bulletin); [Datawrapper CSV](https://datawrapper.dwcdn.net/kSCt4/8787/dataset.csv); [Newsweek](https://newsweek.com/donald-trump-approval-rating-falling-midterm-losses-12709719); [GV Wire](https://gvwire.com/2026/11/16/trump-approval-holds-near-career-low-at-32-reuters-ipsos-poll-finds/); [Democrat & Chronicle](https://eu.democratandchronicle.com/story/news/2026/11/17/donald-trump-approval-rating-latest-polls/92824140007/); [HNGN](https://www.hngn.com/articles/273849/20261116/trump-hits-record-low-32-yougov-averages-sit-higher.htm); [political.org](https://political.org/2026/10/21/trump-approval-hits-new-low-at-36-two-weeks-before-midterms-polls-show/); [Kalshi News](https://news.kalshi.com/p/government-shutdown-odds-december-2026-43-percent); [roic.ai](https://www.roic.ai/news/us-shutdown-risk-rises-as-democrats-weigh-using-funding-deadline-to-challenge-iran-war-11-09-2026); [NOTUS](https://www.notus.org/congress/trump-resumed-the-iran-war-republicans-are-rattled); [Punchbowl](https://punchbowl.news/article/defense/iran-trump-gop/)

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About six weeks remain. The outcome is known once Metaculus checks the CSV on or after Jan 1, 2027. For Yes, some daily "approve" value dated Dec 16 to 31, 2026 must be strictly below every earlier second-term value. Today that bar is 36.25311 (Oct 21). If a lower low is set between now and Dec 15, the bar drops to that value.

(b) Status quo: the latest value is 37.17 (Nov 17), about 0.92 points above the record. If nothing changed, the answer is No.

(c) Base rate: over the past roughly 13 half-month windows (May to mid-November), a new record low was set in about 5 or 6, so roughly 40%. Most of those windows started with the series already at or near its low, though, and none has occurred since Oct 21. Starting from about 0.9 points above the record, a random-walk view gives roughly a 35% chance of breaking 36.25 by Dec 31. It must break the record inside the window and not earlier, which lowers this to roughly 20-25%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The long downtrend runs at about -0.5 points a month, with a new low every 1-2 months from May to October.
- Reuters/Ipsos (Nov 13-16) is stuck at 32%, and Economist/YouGov (Nov 9-11) is at 32%, a series record.
- The average drifted down from 38.35 (Nov 2-8) to 37.17 (Nov 17).
- Funding lapses Dec 11, with about a 44% chance of a shutdown starting Dec 12. That could depress approval right into the window.
- The Iran war and fuel prices are still drags.

Evidence for No:
- No new low has been set since Oct 21, and the series bounced to 38.35 in early November.
- Holiday polling in late December is sparse, so the line often stays flat for days.
- A decline that comes early (late November or early December) would raise the bar for the window itself.
- Kalshi's "below 36% before 2027" price of 0.57 likely tracks a different source; the Silver series has never gone below 36.25.

(e) No scenario: approval hovers at 37-37.5 through December, a short stopgap avoids a shutdown, and holiday polls are sparse, so the line stays flat above 36.25.

Yes scenario: a shutdown starts Dec 12 amid an Iran war escalation and high gas prices. The weekly Reuters and YouGov polls tick down to 31%, and the average slides to about 36.0 around Dec 18-22.

(f) I start from a base of about 22%. Continuing the trend gives about 36.6 by mid-to-late December, so reaching a new low needs roughly 0.4 points of extra negative noise, which is plausible. Shutdown risk timed right before the window nudges the estimate up. Holiday flatness and the requirement that the record fall inside the window nudge it down. No market covers this exact question. These factors roughly cancel, so I stay near 22%.

Probability: 22%

(b) If nothing changes, approval sits near 37.2, about 0.92 points above the record low, and the question resolves No.

(c) Base rate: new lows were set in roughly 4 of the last 6 months. However, any given 16-day window contains a new record far less often. Since May, about 5 or 6 record-setting episodes have occurred over about 180 days, mostly in clusters. Given we start 0.9 points above the record, a specific half-month window holds a new low roughly 20-25% of the time.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- The trend has been down about 0.5 points a month all year.
- Nov 17 was 37.17, drifting down from 38.35 on Nov 2.
- Reuters/Ipsos (Nov 13-16) is stuck at 32%, and YouGov hit a record low of 32% (Nov 9-11).
- The Iran war and fuel prices remain drags.
- A possible shutdown from Dec 12 (Kalshi about 44%) falls just before the window.

Evidence for No:
- The gap of 0.92 points is meaningful.
- There have been no new lows since Oct 21, and the average rebounded after it.
- Holiday polling is sparse, so the line often stays flat for days.
- Any decline in early December resets the bar lower, so the window must hold the absolute minimum.
- Approval sometimes stabilizes or rises slightly in late December.

(e) No scenario: approval drifts between 36.5 and 37.5 through December, Congress passes a stopgap, holiday polling thins out and the line stays flat. Alternatively, a dip to 36.0 happens in early December and the window does not beat it.

Yes scenario: a shutdown from Dec 12, renewed escalation in Iran and higher gas prices push several mid-December polls to new lows, and the average crosses 36.2 around Dec 17-22.

(f) The Kalshi and Polymarket thresholds use different sources and a full-year window, so they are only loose anchors. For example, Kalshi gives 0.57 for approval below 36% before 2027, which suggests material chances of further declines. Starting from about 22%, the downward drift and shutdown risk push up, while the sparse holiday data and the requirement that the window hold the absolute minimum push down. These roughly offset.

Probability: 21%
